svg.text: LensS Collections Intelligence for Optus: technical architecture
One Databricks App in front of governed data, Genie and AI models. Every back-end call runs as the app’s own service principal; people never touch the data.
One HTTPS address per app; one port
Databricks App · Node.js + AppKit · one port
public/ · HTML, JavaScript, CSS · runs in the browser
Then: follow-up suggestions · trace + usage log · streamed to the browser as server-sent events
App identity: the app’s service principal
Reads gold (SELECT) · runs Genie (CAN_RUN) · queries models (CAN_QUERY) · uses Lakebase
· stops itself (CAN_MANAGE on its own app) · no keys in code
Natural language → SQL over 14 gold sources and the metric view. Defined
in code: instructions with rule values filled in, 29 example queries,
Llama 3.3 70B: router, guardrails, follow-ups (org) · GPT-OSS: answer
judge · GTE Large: embeddings for the semantic cache. Smaller models on
Database chatapp-optus: sessions, messages, usage & audit log, answer
cache, cache versions, evaluation cases and runs.
Runs Genie’s SQL and the app’s dashboard, Explorer and cost queries.
Governed data: gold certified views, metric views, rules; plus
system.billing / system.query behind the cost view.
raw tables, as received; N/A and None kept as
ONE-COMMAND DEPLOY (deploy/deploy.py → Databricks CLI, everything as code)
app step: creates or updates the app, binds Genie, warehouse, Lakebase and models; grants the service principal its access; gives readers CAN_USE and demo givers CAN_MANAGE;
shares the app code folder with those who can start it; creates the cost view; checks page scripts; syncs the code and deploys. smoke and routing run only when asked (org).
Own app, schemas (optus_collections_*), Genie space and chat database, so it runs beside LensS Collections in the same workspace without touching it.
